logline: An occasionally true story of Catherine the Great's rise from naive German princess to the most powerful ruler in Russian history - a feminist period black comedy that gleefully ignores factual accuracy in service of something sharper.

renewal.note: Three-season run concluded May 2023. Creator Tony McNamara announced Season 3 as the series finale in August 2023.

bollymeter.basis: 89% RT and universal praise for Elle Fanning and Nicholas Hoult's comedic rapport, plus Tony McNamara's Favourite-adjacent wit applied to a female power fantasy. A sharp debut.

seasons.review_body: The Great premiered May 15, 2020 on Hulu, written by Tony McNamara from his own stage play after his Oscar nomination for The Favourite. The show announces its method in the title card: 'an occasionally true story.' Catherine (Elle Fanning) arrives in Russia as a young bride to Emperor Peter (Nicholas Hoult), finds him a buffoon and a brute, and begins plotting a coup. Critics approved at 89 percent, with reviewers citing the performances - Fanning's comic timing and Hoult's gleeful idiocy - as the engine of a show that uses anachronism and gore in equal measure. The series occupies a specific lane: caustic feminist revisionism via the mode of period farce, and Season 1 owns that lane.

bollymeter.basis: 100% RT - the critical consensus matched Season 1's praise but with stronger overall scores, as the show's satirical ambition deepened alongside the central marriage's genuine complexity.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived November 19, 2021 and achieved a perfect Rotten Tomatoes score, with critics noting the show had matured without softening. The central joke became more complex: Catherine and Peter's marriage moved from adversarial farce into something that required both characters to hold real contradictory feelings. The writing - still McNamara's controlled anachronism and pitch-black humour - earned credit for deepening character without abandoning the comedic scaffolding. Fanning and Hoult's chemistry in scenes that were genuinely funny and genuinely moving simultaneously drew repeated praise. The 100 percent score reflected both the show's consistency and its growing status as one of Hulu's signature critical properties.
seasons.season_over_season: Deepens the central characters beyond farce without losing the show's satirical spine; the perfect RT score reflects a genuine upgrade from an already strong debut.

bollymeter.basis: Another 100% RT score but announced as the final season; the awareness of ending gave the writing a valedictory quality that not all viewers found earned after the show's anarchic first two runs.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 premiered May 12, 2023 and was confirmed as the series finale. Critics sustained the 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes approval, with reviewers treating the concluding season as a well-earned close to a show that had been remarkably consistent across three runs. The season's challenge was structural: Tony McNamara had to navigate an ending while maintaining the anarchic energy that made the first two seasons distinctive. Critics noted success in the character payoffs; some viewer discourse suggested the show's controlled chaos felt slightly tamed by a finale's obligations. Fanning's performance remained the consensus highlight, and the decision to end at three seasons rather than extend was widely credited as editorially sound.
seasons.season_over_season: A valedictory closer that sustains critical momentum while trading some anarchic freedom for earned character conclusions.
